contributions.headingText: Serotonin-producing neuroendocrine tumour (NET) is a well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasm (PanNEN) composed of cells that express serotonin, which in some cases produces carcinoid syndrome, usually after metastasizing to the liver.
2C10.1 & XH7NM1 Neuroendocrine neoplasms of pancreas & Enterochromaffin cell carcinoid (includes serotonin-producing carcinoid)
There is no site predilection within the pancreas; however, ductocentric examples of non-syndromic serotonin-producing neoplasms have been reported {21705949; 22221702}.

Carcinoid syndrome is usually present only when there are liver metastases, but rare cases with carcinoid syndrome without liver metastasis have been reported {28454406}. Most patients with functioning tumours present with atypical carcinoid syndrome, with abdominal pain being the most common symptom (66%), followed by diarrhoea (52%), weight loss (45%), and flushing (34%) {8758239}. Only one case with cardiac valve disease has been reported in the literature {29040196}. The diagnosis is confirmed by demonstrating high urinary 5-HIAA excretion.

Pancreatic serotonin-producing tumours are extremely rare, and those responsible for carcinoid syndrome are even rarer {16104045}. Serotonin-immunoreactive tumours account for 0.58–4.1% of all pancreatic NETs (PanNETs) {21705949; 25602797; 22221702; 28422824}. Only slightly more than 50 well-documented functioning neoplasms have been reported {21705949}. They are more common in females than males. The mean ages of patients with functioning and non-functioning tumours, respectively, are 41 years and 56 years {21705949}.
There are no known etiological factors. No association with genetic syndromes has been documented.

Most are large (1–6 cm {21705949; 16104045}) and do not have distinctive gross features. Functioning tumours are usually larger than non-functioning tumours (mean diameters: 5.2 cm vs 4.2 cm) {21705949}. There have been reports of rare small non-syndromic serotonin-producing tumours centred on the main pancreatic duct that cause dilation of the upstream duct system, mimicking an intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm {21862776; 21431402}.

Most serotonin-producing tumours are well differentiated, G1 or G2 with rare mitosis; very exceptional cases of poorly differentiated neoplasms have been reported {21705949}. However, vascular, perineural, and adjacent organ/structural invasion is frequent, with rare tumour necrosis. Serotonin-producing PanNETs usually do not resemble their intestinal counterparts. The neoplastic cells are frequently arranged in a trabecular pattern and less frequently in solid nests, with variable amounts of stroma {21705949; 22221702}. The stroma is prominent in ductocentric tumours {22221702}. Phenotypically and ultrastructurally, neoplastic cells resemble gastric-type and not intestinal-type enterochromaffin cells (EC cells): unlike their intestinal counterparts, they rarely express substance P, aFGF, VMAT1, and CDX2, but they usually express serotonin and VMAT2 {21705949}. SSTR2A is usually detectable by immunohistochemistry {21705949}.
The cytology is not different from that of typical PanNET. The neoplastic cells contain finely granular cytoplasm and monomorphic round nuclei.
The only genetic alterations described to date are monosomy and rearrangements of chromosome 18 {21705949}.

The staging of serotonin-producing NETs, like that of all PanNENs, follows the eighth editions (2017) of the Union for International Cancer Control (UICC) TNM classification [[Brierly JD, Gospodarowicz MK, Wittekind C, editors. TNM classification of malignant tumours. 8th ed. Oxford (UK): Wiley Blackwell; 2017.]] and the American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) cancer staging manual [[Amin MB, Edge S, Greene F, et al., editors. AJCC cancer staging manual. 8th ed. New York (NY): Springer; 2017.]] {28752469}, which rely on macroscopic assessment of site, tumour size, and metastases. This approach largely corresponds to that of the European Neuroendocrine Tumor Society (ENETS) classification {22525418}. The staging of well-differentiated PanNENs is presented in section Chapter 1.

Serotonin-producing tumours do not differ substantially from non-functioning PanNENs in terms of size, Ki-67 proliferation index, or distant metastases {22221702}. Functioning tumours are associated with a poorer prognosis than non-functioning ones, because they are almost always metastatic {21705949}.
